_comment: Ambience was switched OFF on 2026-09-18 while Joshua had no bed he liked, and back
ON the same day when he supplied one: amb_computer_lab, a real recorded computer
room. Both the browser and the exported mp3 read this switch, so the page and the
file always agree.
To supply more: story-rules/reference/SUPPLYING_AMBIENCE.md. Every supplied file
must carry a credit block -- validation refuses one without it.
Where each kind of sound sits in the finished mix, in dBFS RMS, with the narration
running about -22. scripts/audio.py retune-cues derives every cue gain from these
and the asset's MEASURED level, so a gain survives its asset being regenerated or
renormalised instead of silently becoming wrong.
Set after Joshua listened to the first normalised build and said the sound was
super loud. He was right and the numbers said so: nine cues sat at or above the
narrator's own level, including amb_tombs_array_power_rise -- a bed running under
whole chapters at -21 to -23 dBFS -- and two deep vibrations at -18.8, louder than
the voice. That is what happens when assets are lifted 20 to 27 dB and the gains
that were rescuing them are left in place.
A cue may carry `emphasisDb` in its cue sheet to sit above its category, and the
cue sheet is where such a decision belongs: it is about that moment in the story.
LOWERED 3.1 dB (30% in amplitude) on 2026-09-18: Joshua, on the retuned build, still
found the sound too loud against the voices. Applied to every category so the layer
moves as one and the relationships between cues stay as they were.
LOWERED A FURTHER 6 dB on 2026-09-18, third pass. Joshua, after the 30% cut: SFX
still too loud. Beds now sit about 29 dB under the narration and one-shot events
about 23. If that turns out to be too far, raise these five numbers -- nothing else
needs to change, because every gain is derived from them.
AMBIENCE LOWERED A FURTHER 55% (-6.9 dB) on 2026-09-18 before being switched off,
so that whenever it comes back it starts where Joshua asked rather than where the
last pass left it.
A TONE IS NOT A NOISE, and this table targets RMS as though it were. A 500 Hz sine
at -50 dBFS is plainly audible where a broadband bed at -50 is not, so the sirens
needed roughly 14 dB more attenuation than the table gives -- not because the table
is wrong for beds, but because RMS is a poor predictor for anything tonal. When a
future asset is a tone, expect its emphasisDb to be large and negative.
SUPERSEDED on 2026-09-19 by categoryTargetLufs. Kept as the fallback for an
asset measured before loudness was recorded; the retune report names any cue
still landing on it as 'rms fallback'. When no asset reads that way, delete it.
The DRAMA exports. They were 192 kbps STEREO built from sources that are almost
entirely mono -- paying twice the bitrate for a second channel carrying the same
signal. 96 kbps mono is the same audio at half the size: 36.3 MB becomes about 18.
THE VOICE-ONLY EXPORTS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED. combine joins the clips with
`-c copy`, which is lossless and fast, and re-encoding 500 seconds of narration to
save nine megabytes would spend quality on the one thing the whole project is for.
The silence between clips must also stay at the clips' own format or the copy-join
breaks, which is a good reason not to make that number configurable at all.
Raise these if a stereo mix ever becomes real; nothing else needs to change.
Where each kind of sound sits in the finished mix, in LUFS -- BS.1770
integrated loudness -- with the narration at about -20. scripts/audio.py
retune-cues derives every cue gain from these and the asset's MEASURED
loudness, so a gain survives its asset being regenerated or renormalised.
THIS TABLE REPLACES categoryTargetDbfs, AND ONLY THE MEASURE CHANGED. The
numbers are carried across unaltered on purpose: an asset whose RMS and
loudness agree does not move at all, and the ones that do move are exactly
the ones the old measure was placing wrongly.
Joshua, 2026-09-19: 'The first alarm sound in the first chapter is louder
than the narrator's voice... can't hear him talking.' The cue sheet had it
17 dB under the narration and the file disagreed: sfx_console_alarm_erupt
reads -11.5 dBFS RMS and -5.6 LUFS, so it arrived 5.9 dB louder than the
mix believed. Across the whole set RMS minus LUFS runs from +5.6 to -13.1,
an 18.7 dB spread -- while for speech the two agree within a decibel, which
is why measuring effects against a speech reference by RMS looked right for
as long as it did.
The old note here told a future asset that is a tone to expect a large
negative emphasisDb. That advice stands for the SIRENS, whose RMS and
loudness agree to within 0.1 dB and which are intrusive for reasons
loudness does not measure -- but it was the wrong explanation for the
alerts and notify tones, and those no longer need an emphasis at all.
